Title: Diagnosis of test `testDontQuoteEuroFirstChar`
Details:
The failing test `testDontQuoteEuroFirstChar` expects that when printing a CSV record with a Euro character (representing the Euro symbol, likely Unicode '\u20AC') as the first character of a field using `CSVPrinter` with RFC4180 format, the Euro character field should not be quoted.

Examining the relevant code, we start with `CSVPrinter.printRecord(Object... values)`. It delegates to `CSVFormat.printRecord(Appendable out, Object... values)`, which prints each value by calling the `print(Object value, Appendable out, boolean newRecord)` method for each value while passing a flag indicating the position in the record (first cell or not).

In `CSVFormat.print(Object, Appendable, boolean)`, if a quote character is set (which it is for RFC4180), the `printAndQuote(Object, CharSequence, int, int, Appendable, boolean)` method is called.

The quoted-print logic uses a quote mode, by default `MINIMAL` for RFC4180:
- For the first character in a new record, it checks the character code against a set of conditions. 
- The logic starting at line 1187 checks if the first character in the field `c` falls into certain ranges of ASCII or control characters that should cause quoting:
  ```java
  if (newRecord && (c < 0x20 || c > 0x21 && c < 0x23 || c > 0x2B && c < 0x2D || c > 0x7E)) {
    quote = true;
  }
  ```
- This condition means that if the first character code `c` is less than 0x20 (space) or within certain ranges (between 0x21 and 0x23 exclusive, between 0x2B and 0x2D exclusive, or greater than 0x7E), the value will be quoted.

The Euro symbol (Unicode 0x20AC) is greater than 0x7E, so it enters this condition and causes quoting.

The test expects that the Euro character as the first character should not be quoted (output should be "€" not "\"€\""). The current logic enforces quoting for characters above ASCII ~126, including Euro.

Conclusion: The bug is in the conditional check in `printAndQuote` which is too conservative and causes quoting for characters beyond ASCII range, including the Euro sign, even though quoting is not necessary or expected for these characters per test requirements. The condition needs adjustment to allow such characters to avoid quoting.

---
